summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY (12% constant currency) to INR893 crores, with reported EBITDA of INR294 crores at 33% margin.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached about INR893 crores, up 21% YoY and 12% in constant currency, with forex gains neutral versus Q4. Reported EBITDA was INR294 crores (33%); management says it was about 35% after adding back roughly INR20 crores of one-time TruBridge acquisition costs. PAT was INR193-194 crores, up about 28% YoY. TruBridge closed on July 10, 2026, so Q1 figures are legacy IKS only; management reset TruBridge's steady-state revenue to about $300 million a year (from $340 million pre-close) while keeping its roughly $68 million EBITDA, and reaffirmed a FY30 EBITDA True North of at least INR3,000 crores without further dilution beyond ESOPs.

financial_highlights.change: Adjusted ~INR314 crores (~35%) excluding ~INR20 crores TruBridge acquisition costs
~+28% YoY; higher if adjusted for acquisition costs
QoQ decline attributed to acquisition costs and Abridge mark-to-market uplift via OCI
Legacy IKS guided to 22-23% for rest of FY27
Top 10 vintage ~6 years; top 5 vintage ~7 years
Cash flow hit by one-time NEVA customer payment; not reflected in net debt

segments.name: Legacy IKS (urban/semi-urban, large provider groups)
segments.commentary: Run-rate about $97 million a quarter (~$388 million annualised); management aspires to grow it at 12%+ constant currency. About 600 large provider groups served pre-TruBridge.

segments.name: TruBridge (rural and community EHR)
segments.commentary: Run-rate about $75 million a quarter (~$300 million annualised) after reset from $340 million; ~$68 million EBITDA maintained. Two non-profitable IT and early-out service lines (~$8 million a quarter revenue) to be exited; ~$2-3 million a quarter of customer discounts expected during transformation. Revenue growth outlook not yet given.

guidance_outlook: FY30 True North: at least INR3,000 crores EBITDA, targeted with marginal ESOP dilution only and no return to net debt above pre-TruBridge levels.
Blended EBITDA margin expected to return to early-to-mid 30s from a pro forma 26-27% drop over the next couple of years, via technology, offshore human-in-the-loop, and SG&A synergies.
Legacy IKS aspiration: 12%+ constant-currency growth, explicitly not guidance; TruBridge revenue aspiration to be set after two to three quarters.
Integration expenses expected in Q2 at a similar range to Q1 (~INR20 crores); tax rate guided at 22-23% for legacy IKS.
FY27 expected to remain EPS accretive despite the TruBridge revenue reset, per management.
Management says no acquisitions are ruled out, but INR3,000 crores is achievable without one.
capex_capacity: Headcount inflated above need ahead of TruBridge integration, including investment in TruBridge RCM customers; combined base just over 16,000 employees.
TruBridge acquisition priced at about $550 million for ~$68 million EBITDA, described as accretive.
Five-year lock-in deal signed recently at healthy pricing; no explicit capex figures disclosed.
Patent approved for AAW model (propensity to show/no-show and propensity to pay), deployed in MyCareHub.
demand_pricing: Legacy IKS cross-sell into large health systems showing early land-and-expand wins: Advocate Health Care (top-five US health system, >$35 billion revenue) expanded in RCM and coding; a large California system is moving regions to Epic; a national musculoskeletal aggregator signed a significant RCM deal; StrideCare (vascular) partnership.

Competitive intensity rising; management cites ~30 vendors moving from point solutions to platforms, including Abridge's clinician intelligence launch. Pricing pressure expected but pricing 'not the biggest issue' outside non-deterministic tasks.
Market: total TAM above $260 billion (overall growing ~8%); outsourced TAM ~$35 billion growing ~12%.
Axia Women's Health case study: $12 million cash impact, 96% coding accuracy, reduced denials.
Epic relationship described as strengthening; TruBridge also collaborating with Epic in rural market.

qa_highlights.question: What organic constant-currency growth is healthy over the medium term, and is margin expansion coming from currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin growth is not from currency: revenue grew 12% CC on 4.2% headcount growth; adjusted EBITDA is 35% with neutral forex. Aspiration is 12%+ CC on legacy IKS, not guidance; TruBridge growth to be set in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How does SLM fit with LLMs, and where does glass-box/explainable AI sit?
qa_highlights.answer: Three SLM approaches: standalone SLMs, LLM-distilled SLMs, and hierarchical SLM-plus-LLM. Explainability comes from knowledge graphs acquired via ARAI. Management would not commit to a 60% token-usage reduction, saying it will emerge over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire TruBridge and what criteria govern acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Chosen because the rural market is large, TruBridge holds 30%+ share as one of two dominant rural EHRs, and its service mix resembles ambulatory. Criteria: strategic thesis first, leverage tolerable relative to EBITDA, and accretive price; $68 million EBITDA bought for ~$550 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge's margin of 22-23% fixable, and does the INR3,000 crore target rule out M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers include existing and in-build technology plus offshore human-in-the-loop to restore early-to-mid 30s margins. INR3,000 crores is achievable without another acquisition, but M&A is not ruled out; white space seen as large.

qa_highlights.question: Does Abridge's platform move threaten IKS, and is pricing under pressure in renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management respects Abridge but sees ~30 vendors aspiring to platforms and rising competition. Recent five-year deal signed at healthy price; pricing pressure expected but margin leverage maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge still EPS accretive for FY27 after revenue reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; EBITDA is unchanged, so management says EPS accretion is absolute and possibly a bit higher than previously expected.

risks_watch: TruBridge revenue reset: steady-state revenue cut to about $300 million from $340 million, with ~$8 million a quarter of non-profitable service lines to be exited and ~$2-3 million a quarter of customer discounts during transformation; track whether the $68 million EBITDA holds through the reset.

TruBridge margin recovery: TruBridge runs at a 22-23% margin versus the early-to-mid 30s blended target; progress depends on technology deployment and offshore human-in-the-loop, with management saying it needs two to three quarters to size TruBridge growth.
Integration costs: about INR20 crores of one-time acquisition costs in Q1 and integration expenses expected in Q2 at a similar range; watch reported versus adjusted EBITDA gap.

Competitive intensity: management cites around 30 vendors moving from point solutions to platforms, including Abridge; management expects pricing pressure to rise, though it says pricing is not the biggest issue outside non-deterministic tasks.

Legacy IKS growth versus the 12%+ constant-currency aspiration (Q1 at 12%), with headcount inflated ahead of TruBridge integration; also the INR3,000 crore FY30 True North, which management says is achievable without further acquisitions but does not rule them out.
key_quotes: And so, our commitment to building a single institutionalized culture that is really driven around outcomes, I think one of the things that's coming out as this whole AI hype cycle flushes itself out is that the AI is great as a technology, but if it can't improve outcomes from a cost and quality perspective, then that's not going to be worth it, right?

I wish I could tell you that based on the combination of these approaches, my token utilization will drop by 60% versus a traditional LLM approach. I'm not smart enough to tell you that today, but over a period of time that metric will emerge for us.
So, that's as much as I can tell you is, retaining that 12%-plus growth aspiration constant currency on the IKS book, still wrapping my head around what the TruBridge growth is.
Pricing. Look, I think with increasing competitive intensity, there is always going to be pricing pressure, but I will say that we are signing deals that are very healthy price.
Absolutely, because the good news is even with the revenue reduction, the EBITDA is still the same, and so, absolutely EPS accretive.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the legacy IKS franchise, the Q1 margin and the FY30 True North, which management repeated with a 'good line of sight' framing. Cautious and explicitly non-committal on TruBridge revenue growth, the 60% token-reduction claim, and the 12%+ growth figure, which it calls an aspiration rather than guidance.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 21% YoY (12% constant currency) and management aspires to 12%+ constant-currency growth for legacy IKS, but this is explicitly not guidance, and TruBridge's revenue reset to ~$300M with no growth outlook yet, and no company-built capacity is disclosed.
